followups.problem: The ancestry walk runs `ps` through PATH (execFileSync('ps', ...)). The agent controls PATH in its own environment.
followups.exploit_or_failure: Inside an agent: `env -u CLAUDECODE PATH=/tmp/fakeps:$PATH script -q /dev/null swarm tickets supersede --before X --yes`. Here /tmp/fakeps/ps prints `1` and `bash`. The env markers are gone, the fake ps reports a clean chain, and `script` provides real TTYs, so the gate passes.
followups.fix: Run an absolute path (/bin/ps on macOS and Linux) with a minimal env ({PATH:'/usr/bin:/bin'}). Or read the parent chain without a subprocess (/proc/<pid>/stat on Linux, sysctl KERN_PROC on macOS).

followups.problem: The walk treats any chain that reaches pid 1 as clean. Processes that are orphaned or daemonized get reparented to launchd/init, so the agent drops out of their ancestry.
followups.exploit_or_failure: An agent runs `env -u CLAUDECODE -u SWARM_JOB_ID tmux new-session -d 'swarm tickets supersede --before X --yes'`. A double fork like `(script -q /dev/null swarm ... &)` also works. The tmux server or orphaned `script` is a child of pid 1, so the chain reads zsh -> tmux -> launchd. The pane has a real pty and no markers, so the gate passes. This reopens the 'pty trick' that the CHANGELOG says is closed, using a daemonized pty instead of a direct one.
followups.fix: No same-uid process check can fully stop a determined agent, because it can also edit the ledger or import the module directly. Either describe the gate in docs/CHANGELOG as a guard against accidental or naive agent use, not a security boundary, or require an out-of-band owner confirmation the agent cannot produce (an OS dialog, Touch ID/sudo-style prompt, or a typed nonce from /dev/tty that is not in argv/env). As a cheap hardening step, also refuse when the controlling session leader or terminal is owned by tmux/screen/script started without a login shell.

followups.problem: setSupersedeOwnerCheck is exported from the production module, so any importer can call it. The test spawn helper in tests/tickets-supersede.test.mjs:2020 (diff) already shows the one-line bypass.
followups.exploit_or_failure: `node -e "const m=await import('./tools/scope-commands.mjs'); m.setSupersedeOwnerCheck(()=>null); await m.runScopeCommand(root,'tickets',['supersede','--before','X','--yes'])"` bypasses every check, with no pty or env tricks needed. It is the in-code equivalent of the removed SWARM_OWNER=1.
followups.fix: This is the same same-uid limit as above, so it is not fixable as a hard boundary. To keep it out of the obvious path, move the seam into a test-only module (for example, tests inject via an internal symbol not re-exported from the CLI entry). Document that the gate is advisory against same-user code.

followups.problem: Ancestry matching uses only the `comm` basename. npm-installed agent CLIs can show up as `node` on macOS. The only remaining signal is then the env markers, which the agent can unset.
followups.exploit_or_failure: `env -u CLAUDECODE -u CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT script -q /dev/null swarm tickets supersede ...` from an npm-installed Claude Code on macOS. If `ps -o comm=` reports /usr/local/bin/node for the agent, the chain looks clean.
followups.fix: Also check `ps -o args=` (argv[0]/argv[1] basenames such as .../claude, cli.js under @anthropic-ai/claude-code, @openai/codex). Add a test for a node-hosted agent ancestry.

followups.problem: Possible false refusals for an innocent owner: any ps failure refuses (Windows has no ps, minimal containers may lack it), and a chain that ends in ppid 0 before pid 1 refuses (`docker exec -it`, some sandboxes/WSL).
followups.exploit_or_failure: An owner on Windows, or in `docker exec -it`, cannot run `tickets supersede` or `--set superseded` at all, and has no override now that SWARM_OWNER is gone.
followups.fix: If these platforms are supported, document the limitation or add a platform-specific ancestry reader. Keep failing closed, but print why (for example 'could not inspect process ancestry: ps unavailable').

followups.problem: Only the classic pages keep `Cache-Control: no-store`. The Command Center HTML response loaded via `?t=TOKEN` (which also carries the Set-Cookie with the token) and /api/command-center JSON are now `no-cache` without `private`.
followups.exploit_or_failure: There is no auth bypass: auth runs before any 304, so a revalidation without a token gets 403. But the browser now writes the token-bearing URL and board JSON to its disk cache, and a shared cache in front of a remote tunnel is allowed to store them. The perf gain on a single HTML document is negligible.
followups.fix: Send `no-store` on any response that sets the cookie or was requested with `?t=`, and `private, no-cache` on API JSON. Keep `public` caching for static JS/CSS/fonts only.

followups.problem: After the 2 s TTL, the snapshot cache reuses the previously encoded body whenever `[snapshot.version, snapshot.at]` is unchanged. This assumes every visible change bumps version or `at`.
followups.exploit_or_failure: If the real board's `at` is a ledger mtime and `version` is a schema version, changes from run folders, orchestrator sessions or agent counts that don't touch the ledger are served stale indefinitely, both as a 200 with old data and as a 304. The fixture always bumps `revision`, so the test can't catch this. versionInfo() changes are also never reflected.
followups.fix: Confirm that board.snapshot's `at` is the generation time. Otherwise drop the revision short-circuit and hash the freshly built payload. The ETag/304 still saves the bytes.

followups.problem: The Cockpit paint signature includes only id/name/ledger/sessions/meta/done/total/runStream plus the minute bucket. The fixture shape puts sessions under `orchestrator.sessions`, and headerCounters(p)/runStreamItems(p, orch) may read other fields.
followups.exploit_or_failure: An orchestrator or agent state change that lives outside the signed fields isn't repainted until the minute rolls over or the ledger changes. That means up to 60 s of stale Cockpit status on a 5 s poll.
followups.fix: Sign the whole project payload (JSON.stringify(p)) plus the minute bucket. The cost is trivial next to the DOM work it saves.

followups.problem: reconcileDom keeps existing live elements and discards the freshly rendered ones, along with any listeners the render attached. Unkeyed rows (no data-ticket-id/data-project-id) in hive-panels, the Cockpit columns and the worker cards keep handlers that close over the first render's data.
followups.exploit_or_failure: If any panel row's click or tooltip handler captures per-row data and the row at index i later represents a different item, the action targets the old item. Keyed cards and tickets are safe, and the browser fixture only checks a keyed ticket title.
followups.fix: Audit the hive-panels, renderTicketColumn, renderWorkerCards and renderStackSummaryTiles handlers. Either make them read data-* attributes at event time (delegation) or replace elements whose handlers differ. Add a test that reorders unkeyed rows and clicks one.

followups.problem: The only timing and CPU budgets (idle < 5%, switch < 150 ms) are in an opt-in test that is skipped unless SWARM_CC_BROWSER_PERF is set, and SWARM_CC_PERF_BASELINE disables the asserts. The default suite checks structure and gzip size only, so it passes while slow.
followups.exploit_or_failure: A regression that brings back a 60 fps loop or a blocking Cockpit await passes `npm test`. Only the ambient-motion unit test (frame cap and pause) and static import checks would catch some of it.
followups.fix: Run the browser perf test in the release gate (the merge checklist) with SWARM_CC_BROWSER_PERF=1, or record `npm run perf:cc` output per train. Also wait for two rAFs after `.cc-cockpit-shell h1`, to match the harness definition.

followups.problem: The CHANGELOG and train notes claim gzip/brotli, but watch-server only implements gzip (gzipSync). The test sends `br, gzip` and expects gzip.
followups.exploit_or_failure: The release note is inaccurate. There's no functional impact.
followups.fix: Change the text to 'gzip', or add brotli with its own ETag suffix.

followups.problem: The new `if (!streamEverClosed) return;` in the idle/shutdown interval skips the rest of the callback. The diff shows only 3 lines of trailing context, so I couldn't confirm that nothing after the finished-run check (for example other idle-shutdown paths) needed to run before a stream has ever closed.
followups.exploit_or_failure: If later code in that callback handles 'never opened a stream' idle shutdown, a server that nobody ever opened would no longer exit.
followups.fix: Confirm the rest of the callback only matters after a stream has closed, or narrow the early return to just the getRunSnapshot call. (The line number refers to the diff file, not the source.)

summary: No blockers. Owner gate: this is a real improvement over main. SWARM_OWNER=1 is gone. Markers are checked first, and any defined value, including empty, refuses. The ancestry walk fails closed on errors, loops, the hop limit and bad ppids. Both stdin and stdout must be TTYs. `--set superseded` now runs the gate before --dry-run and before the confirmation flags, and both paths use the same gate. A naive or accidental agent call, SWARM_OWNER=1, and a pty opened directly under the agent are now refused. But to answer the owner's question directly: a deliberate same-user agent can still get through. It can (a) daemonize or orphan a pty via tmux/screen or a double-forked `script`, so the chain ends at pid 1, (b) shadow `ps` on PATH, (c) import the module and call the exported setSupersedeOwnerCheck, or (d) on some setups show up as `node`. Each needs the agent to also unset its env markers. No same-uid check can close this completely, so I've logged these as follow-ups rather than blockers. The fixes are: run ps by absolute path, also check process args, keep the test seam out of the public export, and either describe the gate as a guard against accidental agent use or add out-of-band owner confirmation. Perf/serve: SECURITY headers and the exact CSP are spread into every response, including 304s and gzip responses. The 304 path runs after token, remote-identity and funnel checks (the tests cover this). Cookie semantics are unchanged. The snapshot cache key covers the pathname and every effective query option, with `t` removed and redact forced to true, so there is no cross-query leakage. In-flight requests are coalesced and the cache is capped at 128 entries. SSE is excluded from compression. The perf script redacts the `t=` token in the URL field, errors and console output, and contains no hard-coded secrets. The lazy Cockpit, tour and palette loads, the modulepreload warm-up, the parked Hive, and the frame-capped ambient motion with hidden, offscreen, reduced-motion and 5 s idle pauses all look correct in the code. I couldn't verify a few risks from the diff alone: the snapshot cache trusts the board's version/at revision, the Cockpit's partial paint signature can leave status up to 60 s stale, Command Center HTML/API dropped from no-store to no-cache, and reconciliation keeps old handlers on unkeyed rows. The timing and CPU budgets only run opt-in. All of these are follow-ups.
